title: SpaceX's science fiction dreams come with an astronomical bill
excerpt: SpaceX shares fell as much as 11% in overnight trading despite the company delivering an earnings beat on Tuesday.
content_html:
By Tom Carter

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

and Lloyd Lee

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

As an abandoned SpaceX rocket crashes into the moon, Elon Musk's science-fiction ambitions are on their own collision course with Wall Street.

SpaceX shares fell as much as 11% in after-hours trading despite the company delivering an earnings beat on Tuesday, as investors expressed anxiety over the astronomical bill for Musk's vision of an AI-powered, space-bound future.

The rocket company, which raised a record-breaking $86 billion in its June IPO, reported that quarterly revenue had soared 92% from a year earlier to $7.8 billion, above analyst expectations.

SpaceX also nearly halved its net loss to $541 million, and reported surging revenue from its AI business after striking a series of compute deals with Anthropic and Google.

It's the amount the company is spending on AI infrastructure, however, that is making investors jittery: nearly $16 billion for the quarter, well above the $13 billion Wall Street was expecting and more than double the previous quarter.

SpaceX is the latest tech giant to face backlash over its AI spending in recent weeks, with Tesla and Google's shares also falling after they reported higher-than-expected capex spending.

'I know this sounds totally nuts'

On the analyst call following the earnings, Musk and SpaceX's other executives justified the eye-watering spending as necessary to achieve the cosmic goals that were a staple of the company's pitch to investors in its record-breaking public offering.

The world's richest man suggested that Starlink, SpaceX's booming connectivity business, would soar to new heights by providing bandwidth for humanoid robots — presumably built by Tesla — on Earth and beyond.

"Using robots on the moon to scale up manufacturing on the moon — which sounds super sci-fi right now, but it's going to happen — will enable us to build the mass accelerator on the moon," Musk told investors. A mass accelerator is a proposed electromagnetic launch slingshot used to catapult objects into space.

"If you have a mass accelerator on the moon, I know this sounds totally nuts, but you can probably scale to a thousand times the economy of Earth in terms of intelligence launched to space, maybe even a million times," the former trillionaire added.

Musk predicted that SpaceX could hit $1 trillion in revenue as early as 2029, bringing the target forward from 2031, and said the company plans to begin launching its orbital data centers, which SpaceX has dubbed Starmind, next year.

"This is not some sort of far future distant thing," he added.

CFO Bret Johnsen said that SpaceX's overall capex spend would likely be "very similar" for the next two quarters — implying that it could reach $65 billion this year — but added that SpaceX's AI infrastructure was paying for itself almost as quickly as the company can build it.

"Specifically on the AI compute side, we're able to deploy capital in such a way that we're getting less than a one-year payback," Johnsen said.

In a note on Wednesday, UBS analysts raised revenue estimates for 2026 and 2027 on the back of the outperformance of the company's AI business, and wrote that SpaceX was "hitting on all cylinders."

SpaceX stock's bumpy ride

Investor nerves over rising AI bills have only added to the uncertainty surrounding SpaceX's share price, which is now trading about 16% below the IPO price after collapsing over the past month.

The volatility is likely to continue, with around $100 billion worth of shares set to become available for sale on Thursday after the expiry of the first lock-up period for early SpaceX investors and employees.

Even with the uncertainty, SpaceX's first earnings as a public company were a reminder that the company's underlying business is still formidable. Revenue for Starlink, SpaceX's main moneymaker, came in well ahead of Wall Street's expectations, and the company said that enterprise and government revenue for Starlink grew by more than 108% year-over-year in the last quarter.

SpaceX is also coming off two successful launches of its massive Starship rocket, which is critical for Musk's ambitious vision for moving data centers and manufacturing into orbit.

Musk pointed out on the analyst call that even without Starship, SpaceX delivers vastly more material into orbit than the rest of the world combined. The billionaire told investors that SpaceX's engineering prowess meant that its competitors building data centers had little chance of competing, on Earth or in space.

"This is like, frankly, the New York Yankees going in and playing a little league team," said Musk. "It's kind of ridiculous."

作者：Tom Carter 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 和 Lloyd Lee 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

当一枚废弃的 SpaceX 火箭坠入月球时，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的科幻野心正在与华尔街发生碰撞。

尽管 SpaceX 周二公布的业绩好于预期，但该公司股价在盘后交易中仍下跌了 11%，原因是投资者对马斯克关于人工智能驱动的太空未来愿景的天文数字费用表示焦虑。

这家火箭公司在 6 月份的 IPO 中筹集了创纪录的 860 亿美元资金，该公司报告称，季度收入较上年同期飙升 92%，达到 78 亿美元，高于分析师预期。

SpaceX 还将其净亏损减少了近一半，至 5.41 亿美元，并报告称，在与 Anthropic 和谷歌达成一系列计算交易后，其人工智能业务收入大幅增长。

然而，令投资者感到不安的是该公司在人工智能基础设施上的支出：该季度接近 160 亿美元，远高于华尔街预期的 130 亿美元，是上一季度的两倍多。

SpaceX 是最近几周因其人工智能支出而面临强烈反对的最新科技巨头，特斯拉和谷歌的股价也在报告高于预期的资本支出后下跌。

“我知道这听起来很疯狂”

在财报发布后的分析师电话会议上，马斯克和 SpaceX 的其他高管表示，为了实现宇宙目标，这笔令人眼花缭乱的支出是必要的，而这些目标是该公司在破纪录的公开发行中向投资者宣传的主要内容。

这位世界首富表示，SpaceX 蓬勃发展的连接业务 Starlink 将通过为地球及其他地方的人形机器人（可能是特斯拉制造的）提供带宽而飙升至新的高度。

马斯克告诉投资者：“在月球上使用机器人来扩大月球制造规模——这现在听起来很科幻，但它将会发生——将使我们能够在月球上建造质量加速器。” 质量加速器是一种拟议的电磁发射弹弓，用于将物体弹射到太空。

这位前万亿富翁补充道：“如果你在月球上有一个质量加速器，我知道这听起来完全疯狂，但就向太空发射的情报而言，你的经济规模可能是地球的一千倍，甚至可能是一百万倍。”

马斯克预测，SpaceX 的收入最早可能在 2029 年达到 1 万亿美元，将这一目标从 2031 年提前，并表示该公司计划明年开始启动其轨道数据中心，SpaceX 将其称为 Starmind。

“这不是什么遥远的未来的事情，”他补充道。

首席财务官布雷特·约翰森 (Bret Johnsen) 表示，SpaceX 未来两个季度的总体资本支出可能“非常相似”，这意味着今年可能达到 650 亿美元，但他补充说，SpaceX 的人工智能基础设施的收回成本几乎与公司建设速度一样快。

约翰森说：“特别是在人工智能计算方面，我们能够以不到一年的时间就收回投资的方式部署资本。”

在周三的一份报告中，由于该公司人工智能业务表现出色，瑞银分析师上调了 2026 年和 2027 年的收入预期，并写道 SpaceX 正在“全力以赴”。

SpaceX 股票走势坎坷

投资者对不断上涨的人工智能账单感到紧张，这只会增加 SpaceX 股价的不确定性，在过去一个月暴跌后，该公司目前的股价较 IPO 价格低约 16%。

这种波动可能会持续下去，在 SpaceX 早期投资者和员工的第一个禁售期结束后，周四将有价值约 1000 亿美元的股票可供出售。

尽管存在不确定性，SpaceX 作为上市公司的首次盈利提醒人们，该公司的基础业务仍然强大。 SpaceX 的主要赚钱工具 Starlink 的收入远远超出了华尔街的预期，该公司表示，上季度 Starlink 的企业和政府收入同比增长超过 108%。

SpaceX 还成功发射了两次大型 Starship 火箭，这对于马斯克将数据中心和制造业转移到轨道的雄心勃勃的愿景至关重要。

马斯克在分析师电话会议上指出，即使没有 Starship，SpaceX 向轨道运送的物质也比世界其他地方的总和要多得多。 这位亿万富翁告诉投资者，SpaceX 的工程实力意味着其建设数据中心的竞争对手在地球或太空上几乎没有竞争的机会。

“坦率地说，这就像纽约洋基队进入并与一支小联盟球队比赛一样，”马斯克说。 “这有点荒谬。”
